definition: keyword_overlap — recall of the input's content terms in the output: at least 35% of the input's content terms must appear in the output (config key keyword_overlap, default 0.35). Content terms: words longer than two characters that are not stopwords or request verbs; code identifiers and paths are split into their words; inflections are folded. Definition version: docs/api-reference.md §Relevance Rules and the rule description as merged in #416 (9d9fd50) on 2026-09-04. Positive = fewer than 35% of the input's content terms present (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-04. Held out on 2026-09-23: the 9 case(s) copied from, varied from or modelled on the 24 real transcripts in tests/fixtures/real-transcripts (overlap-001, overlap-002, overlap-003, overlap-004, overlap-005, overlap-006, overlap-007, overlap-008, overlap-009) were removed, so no number this family publishes is estimated on a transcript, and the transcript line in proof/TRANSCRIPTS.md and proof/COMPOSITE.md is measured on cases none of these rates were estimated from. 3 replacement case(s), authored the same day and marked in their notes, bring the family back to the 24-case floor the runner enforces. The replacements sit far from the threshold (0% or 100% under any reasonable reading), so their labels do not depend on this file's particular stopword or sentence lists.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition on 2026-09-04. First labelled that morning against the definition then documented (20% of unique words longer than two characters); re-labelled the same day, after #416 replaced it, against the 35%-of-content-terms definition. The label is the documented formula applied independently by script whose stopword list, request-verb list and inflection folding are this file's own reading of the definition, not the rule's lists; each note states the count that decided the label. 5 case(s) fell within seven points of the threshold under that reading and were dropped as undecidable from the documentation alone: t-13 (38%); t-24 (40%); t-08 (39%); t-19 (33%); t-23 (29%).
